lines: Hunting for a job late last year, lawyer Gant Redmon **stumbled across** CareerBuilder, a job database on the Internet. He searched it with no success but was attracted by the site's "personal search agent". It's an interactive feature that lets visitors key in job criteria such as location, title, and salary, then E-mails them when a matching position is posted in the database. Redmon chose the keywords legal, intellectual property, and Washington, D.C. Three weeks later, he got his first **notification** of an opening. "I **struck gold**," says Redmon, who E-mailed his resume to the employer and won a position as in-house counsel for a company.

去年年底找工作时，律师甘特·雷德蒙偶然发现了互联网上的求职数据库 CareerBuilder。他搜索了一番，虽然没有找到合适的工作，却被网站的“个人搜索代理”吸引住了。这是一项互动功能：求职者可以输入地点、职位、薪资等条件，数据库中一旦发布匹配的职位，系统便会发邮件通知他们。雷德蒙选定的关键词是“法律”“知识产权”和“华盛顿特区”。三周后，他收到了第一份职位空缺通知。“我可捡到宝了，”雷德蒙说；他把简历通过电子邮件发给雇主，最终获得了一家公司的内部法律顾问职位。

lines: With thousands of career-related sites on the Internet, finding promising openings can be time-consuming and inefficient. Search agents reduce the need for repeated visits to the databases. But although a search agent worked for Redmon, career experts see **drawbacks**. Narrowing your criteria, for example, may work against you: "Every time you answer a question you **eliminate** a possibility," says one expert.
互联网上与求职相关的网站数以千计，要找到有前景的空缺职位可能既费时又低效。搜索代理减少了反复访问资料库的必要。不过，虽然搜索代理帮雷德蒙找到了工作，求职专家们却看到了其中的缺点。例如，把自己的标准定得太窄可能对你不利：“每回答一个问题，你就排除了一种可能性，”一位专家说。

lines: For any job search, you should start with a narrow concept -- what you think you want to do -- then broaden it. "None of these programs do that," says another expert. "There's no career counseling implicit in all of this." Instead, the best strategy is to use the agent as a kind of **tip service** to keep **abreast of** jobs in a particular database; when you get E-mail, consider it a reminder to check the database again. "I would not rely on agents for finding everything that is added to a database that might interest me," says the author of a job-searching guide.
无论找什么工作，都应当从一个较窄的设想——自己认为想做什么——出发，然后逐步扩大范围。“这些程序没有一个能做到这一点，”另一位专家说。“这些功能中根本不包含职业咨询。”相反，最佳做法是把搜索代理当作一种信息提示服务，用来随时了解某个数据库中的职位信息；收到邮件时，就把它视作再次查看数据库的提醒。“我不会指望搜索代理替我找到数据库中新增的、所有可能令我感兴趣的信息，”一本求职指南的作者说。

lines: Some sites design their agents to **tempt** job hunters to return. When CareerSite's agent sends out messages to those who have signed up for its service, for example, it includes only three potential jobs -- those it considers the best matches. There may be more matches in the database; job hunters will have to visit the site again to find them -- and they do. "On the day after we send our messages, we see a sharp increase in our traffic," says Seth Peets, vice president of marketing for CareerSite.
有些网站设计代理程序是为了引诱求职者回访。例如，当CareerSite的代理向注册了其服务的用户发送信息时，其中只包含三个潜在的工作职位——即它认为最匹配的那三个。资料库里可能还有更多匹配的职位，求职者只好再次访问该网站去寻找——而他们也确实会这么做。“在发出信息后的第二天，我们的访问量就会急剧增加，”CareerSite营销副总裁塞思·皮茨说。

lines: Even those who aren't hunting for jobs may find search agents worthwhile. Some use them to keep a close watch on the demand for their line of work or gather information on compensation to **arm** themselves when negotiating for a raise. Although happily employed, Redmon maintains his agent at CareerBuilder. "You always keep your eyes open," he says. Working with a personal search agent means having another set of eyes looking out for you.
即使那些不找工作的人也可能发现搜索代理是有价值的。有些人利用它们密切关注本行业的需求情况，或者搜集薪酬方面的信息，以便在协商加薪时为自己增加筹码。尽管雷德蒙工作干得很开心，他仍保留着他在CareerBuilder的搜索代理。“你要时刻保持警惕，”他说。使用个人搜索代理，就意味着多了一双眼睛在替你留意机会。

lines: Over the past century, all kinds of unfairness and discrimination have been condemned or made illegal. But one **insidious** form continues to thrive: **alphabetism**. This, for those as yet unaware of such a disadvantage, refers to discrimination against those whose surnames begin with a letter in the lower half of the alphabet.
在过去的一个世纪里，各种各样的不公正和歧视都遭到了谴责，或者被定为非法。但是有一种隐蔽的歧视形式却继续盛行：字母顺序主义。所谓字母顺序主义——对于尚未意识到这种劣势的人来说——指的是对那些姓氏以字母表后半部分字母开头的人的歧视。

lines: It has long been known that a taxi firm called AAAA cars has a big advantage over Zodiac cars when customers thumb through their phone directories. Less well known is the advantage that Adam Abbott has in life over Zoe Zysman. English names are fairly evenly spread between the halves of the alphabet. Yet a **suspiciously** large number of top people have surnames beginning with letters between A and K.

lines: Thus the American president and vice-president have surnames starting with B and C respectively; and 26 of George Bush's predecessors (including his father) had surnames in the first half of the alphabet against just 16 in the second half. Even more striking, six of the seven heads of government of the G7 rich countries are alphabetically advantaged (Berlusconi, Blair, Bush, Chirac, Chretien and Koizumi). The world's three top central bankers (Greenspan, Duisenberg and Hayami) are all close to the top of the alphabet, even if one of them really uses Japanese characters. As are the world's five richest men (Gates, Buffett, Allen, Ellison and Albrecht).

例如，美国总统和副总统的姓氏分别以B和C开头；乔治·布什的前任总统中（包括他的父亲），有26位的姓氏在字母表的前半部分，而只有16位在后半部分。更令人瞩目的是，西方七大富裕国政府的七位首脑中有六位在字母排序上占了便宜（贝卢斯科尼、布莱尔、布什、希拉克、克雷蒂安和小泉）。世界三大中央银行家（格林斯潘、德伊森贝赫和速水优）的姓氏也都在字母表前列，尽管其中一位实际上用的是日本文字。世界五大首富（盖茨、巴菲特、艾伦、埃里森和阿尔布雷希特）也是如此。

lines: Can this merely be coincidence? One theory, dreamt up in all the spare time enjoyed by the alphabetically disadvantaged, is that **the rot sets in early**. At the start of the first year in infant school, teachers seat pupils alphabetically from the front, to make it easier to remember their names. So short-sighted Zysman junior gets stuck in the back row, and is rarely asked the **improving** questions posed by those insensitive teachers. lines: When it comes to the slowing economy, Ellen Spero isn't **biting her nails** just yet. But the 47-year-old **manicurist** isn't cutting, filing or polishing as many nails as she'd like to, either. Most of her clients spend $12 to $50 weekly, but last month two longtime customers suddenly stopped showing up. Spero blames the softening economy. "I'm a good economic indicator," she says. "I provide a service that people can do without when they're concerned about saving some dollars." So Spero is downscaling, shopping at middle-brow Dillard's department store near her suburban Cleveland home, instead of Neiman Marcus. "I don't know if other clients are going to abandon me, too," she says.

说起经济放缓，艾伦·斯佩罗暂时还没有紧张得坐立不安。不过，这位47岁的美甲师也确实没有接到她所期望的那么多修剪、锉磨和抛光指甲的业务。她的大多数顾客每周花费12至50美元，但上个月，两名老顾客突然不再光顾。斯佩罗把这归因于经济走弱。“我是一个很好的经济晴雨表，”她说。“我提供的这项服务，是人们想省点钱时可以省去的。”因此，斯佩罗也在降低消费档次，改到克利夫兰郊区家附近的中档迪拉德百货购物，不再去内曼·马库斯百货。“我不知道其他顾客是否也会不再光顾，”她说。

lines: Even before Alan Greenspan's admission that America's red-hot economy is cooling, lots of working folks had already seen signs of the slowdown themselves. From car **dealerships** to Gap outlets, sales have been lagging for months as shoppers temper their spending. For retailers, who last year took in 24 percent of their revenue between Thanksgiving and Christmas, the cautious approach is coming at a crucial time. Already, experts say, holiday sales are off 7 percent from last year's pace. But don't sound any alarms just yet. Consumers seem only mildly concerned, not panicked, and many say they remain optimistic about the economy's long-term prospects even as they do some modest belt-tightening.

早在艾伦·格林斯潘承认美国过热的经济开始降温之前，许多上班族自己就已经看到了经济放缓的迹象。从汽车经销店到 Gap 门店，随着顾客节制开支，销售已连续数月表现疲弱。对零售商来说，去年他们在感恩节到圣诞节之间赚取了全年24%的收入，而消费者在这个关键时刻却变得谨慎起来。专家们说，节日期间销售额已经比去年下降了7%。不过目前还用不着拉响警报。消费者似乎只是略有担忧而没有恐慌，许多人说，即使稍稍勒紧裤腰带，他们对经济的长期前景依然保持乐观。

lines: Americans today don't place a very high value on intellect. Our heroes are athletes, entertainers, and entrepreneurs, not scholars. Even our schools are where we send our children to get a practical education -- not to pursue knowledge for the sake of knowledge. Symptoms of **pervasive** anti-intellectualism in our schools aren't difficult to find.
如今的美国人并不太看重才智。我们的英雄是运动员、演艺人员和企业家，而不是学者。甚至学校也只是我们送孩子去接受实用教育的地方——而不是为了知识本身去追求知识。学校中反才智主义的普遍症状并不难找到。

lines: "Intellect is resented as a form of power or privilege," writes historian and professor Richard Hofstadter in Anti-Intellectualism in American Life, a Pulitzer-Prize winning book on the roots of anti-intellectualism in US politics, religion, and education. From the beginning of our history, says Hofstadter, our democratic and **populist** urges have driven us to reject anything that smells of **elitism**. Practicality, common sense, and native intelligence have been considered more noble qualities than anything you could learn from a book.
“才智被人们当作权力或特权而憎恶，”历史学家理查德·霍夫施塔特教授在《美国生活中的反才智主义》一书中写道——这本普利策奖获奖著作探讨了美国政治、宗教和教育中反才智主义的根源。霍夫施塔特说，从我们的历史之初，我们对民主和民粹主义的渴望就驱使我们拒绝任何带有精英主义味道的东西。务实、常识和天赋的智力一直被认为比从书本里能学到的任何东西都更为高贵。

lines: Ralph Waldo Emerson and other Transcendentalist philosophers thought schooling and rigorous book learning put unnatural restraints on children: "We are shut up in schools and college recitation rooms for 10 or 15 years and come out at last with a bellyful of words and do not know a thing." Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn exemplified American anti-intellectualism. Its hero avoids being civilized -- going to school and learning to read -- so he can preserve his **innate** goodness.
拉尔夫·瓦尔多·爱默生和其他超验主义哲学家认为，学校教育和刻板的书本学习给孩子们强加了不自然的束缚：“我们被关在学校和大学的背诵室里10年或15年，出来时满腹词句，却什么都不懂。”马克·吐温笔下的哈克贝利·费恩正是美国人反才智主义的典型。书中主人公逃避被“文明化”——逃避上学和读书识字——以便保住他天生的善良本性。

lines: Intellect, according to Hofstadter, is different from native intelligence, a quality we reluctantly admire. Intellect is the critical, creative, and **contemplative** side of the mind. lines: Many theories concerning the causes of juvenile delinquency (crimes committed by young people) focus either on the individual or on society as the major contributing influence. lines: Families have also **experienced** changes these years. lines: Only recently did linguists begin the serious study of languages that were very different from their own. Two anthropologist-linguists, Franz Boas and Edward Sapir, were pioneers in describing many native languages of North and South America during the first half of the twentieth century. (42) We are obliged to them because some of these languages have since vanished, as the peoples who spoke them died out or became assimilated and lost their native languages. Other linguists in the earlier part of this century, however, who were less eager to deal with bizarre data from "exotic" language, were not always so grateful. (43) The newly described languages were often so strikingly different from the well studied languages of Europe and Southeast Asia that some scholars even accused Boas and Sapir of fabricating their data. Native American languages are indeed different, so much so in fact that Navajo could be used by the US military as a code during World War II to send secret messages.

直到最近，语言学家们才开始认真研究与他们自己的语言截然不同的语言。在20世纪上半叶，弗朗兹·博厄斯和爱德华·萨丕尔这两位人类学家兼语言学家是描述南北美洲许多土著语言的先驱。（42）我们之所以感激他们，是因为其中有些语言从此已经消失，原因是说这些语言的部族或是消亡了，或是被同化而丧失了自己的本族语言。然而，本世纪早期其他一些语言学家并不那么热心处理来自“异域”语言的怪异资料，因此他们并不总是心存感激。（43）这些新近被描述的语言与已经得到充分研究的欧洲和东南亚语言往往有着惊人的差别，以至于有些学者甚至指责博厄斯和萨丕尔编造了资料。美洲土著语言的确是独特的，其独特程度之高，以至于纳瓦霍语在第二次世界大战期间曾被美军用作密码来传递机密信息。

lines: Sapir's pupil, Benjamin Lee Whorf, continued the study of American Indian languages. (44) Being interested in the relationship of language and thought, Whorf developed the idea that the structure of language determines the structure of habitual thought in a society. He reasoned that because it is easier to formulate certain concepts and not others in a given language, the speakers of that language think along one track and not along another. (45) Whorf came to believe in a sort of linguistic determinism which, in its strongest form, states that language imprisons the mind, and that the grammatical patterns in a language can produce far-reaching consequences for the culture of a society. Later, this idea became to be known as the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, but this term is somewhat inappropriate. Although both Sapir and Whorf emphasized the diversity of languages, Sapir himself never explicitly supported the notion of linguistic determinism.

data.title: 终点又是新起点（The Finishing Line Is a New Starting Point）
data.directions_en: Study the following drawing carefully and write an essay in which you should 1) describe the drawing, 2) interpret its meaning, and 3) support your view with examples. You should write about 200 words neatly on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points)
data.directions_zh: 仔细观察下图，写一篇文章，内容包括：1）描述图画；2）解释其含义；3）用例子支持你的观点。应在答题卡2上工整地写约200词。（20分）
sample: As is vividly shown in the drawing, a young runner, sweat streaming down his face, has just crossed the finishing line of a race. Instead of stopping to rest, however, he is looking ahead with determination, for the caption beneath the picture tells us: "The finishing line is also a new starting point."
正如图画生动地描绘的那样，一位年轻的赛跑运动员满脸汗水，刚刚冲过比赛的终点线。然而他并没有停下来休息，而是目光坚定地望向前方，因为图下的文字告诉我们：“终点又是新起点。”

sample: The drawing conveys a profound meaning: an achievement should never be the end of our efforts, but the beginning of a new journey. Life is an endless course of striving. If one rests content with what he has accomplished, he will soon be overtaken by those who keep pressing forward. History provides numerous examples. Thomas Edison never paused after his invention of the light bulb but went on to obtain more than a thousand patents; the Chinese athletes who won gold medals at the Olympics immediately set their sights on the next games. Their stories all prove that the true spirit of success lies in taking every ending as a fresh start.
这幅图画蕴含着深刻的含义：一项成就绝不应是我们努力的终点，而应是新征程的起点。人生是一场永无止境的拼搏。如果一个人满足于已有的成绩，很快就会被那些不断奋进的人超越。历史上不乏这样的例子。托马斯·爱迪生发明电灯后从未停步，继而取得了一千多项专利；在奥运会上夺得金牌的中国运动员们，立刻又把目光投向下一届赛会。他们的事迹都证明：成功的真谛就在于把每一个终点当作新的起点。
